message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering the 24-hour window ending 2026-07-11 05:10 IST (2026-07-10 23:40 UTC). One relevant new item was confirmed: Ubuntu published several Linux kernel security notices on 10 July 2026. I did not find confirmed new vulnerabilities for the other monitored products, including MongoDB-family components, FortiOS/FortiGate, SonicWall, Cisco Nexus/UCS/Fabric Extender, VMware ESXi/vCenter/Tools, Microsoft products, Adobe products, Chrome stable, Firefox, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, OpenSSL, Apache HTTP Server, Tomcat, Nginx, Veeam, Tenable Nessus, Grafana, WordPress/Yoast/ACF, or Cato Networks within this run window.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Ubuntu / Linux kernel packages
- Issue: Ubuntu Security Notices USN-8530-1, USN-8529-1, USN-8528-1, USN-8527-1, and USN-8492-5
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu in the notices reviewed.
- Description: Canonical published multiple Ubuntu kernel updates on 10 July 2026. The notices include fixes for Dirty Frag and Fragnesia-style Linux kernel flaws that may allow local privilege escalation or possible container escape, along with additional kernel subsystem flaws that Ubuntu says could possibly be used to compromise affected systems.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes Ubuntu. The notices apply to Ubuntu kernel packages across specific release/flavor combinations, including Ubuntu 18.04 LTS AWS/cloud kernels, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS Raspberry Pi and Xilinx ZynqMP kernels, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS FIPS kernels.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Possible matches needing review**

- MongoDB family: I searched MongoDB server, mongod, mongos, Atlas, Ops Manager, drivers, connectors, GitHub advisory, and NVD-style terms. I found MongoDB advisories from June 2026 and earlier, but no credible new MongoDB-family item in the last 24 hours.
- Cato Networks: The advisory page lists CVE-2026-12374 for the Cato macOS Client, which maps to the monitored Cato Networks product family, but the vendor page shows it was updated on 1 July 2026, so it is outside this run window and excluded from confirmed findings.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Ubuntu hosts that match the affected kernel package families. For the rest of the monitored list, no fresh, credible, product-matched vulnerability was confirmed in the last 24 hours.
